I'd like to get started in making things out of wood. Where do you suggest I start and how much do you think it would cost?
Do you think I should make it out of one plank of wood, or be adventurous and make one out of smaller pieces?

Smaller pieces, you'll get some practice with gluing ups and making the boards true and what not. The glue you want to use is called Titebond 3. The wood you want to use should be like maple or walnut. A decent rule of thumb for stuff that is going to come into contact with food is that you want to the wood to come from a tree that produces something you eat. Like maple syrup, or walnuts.

I agree that you should start with something small like a cutting board, but if you want to get into a smaller furniture project like a side table, a good place to start is with some inexpensive pine. You can afford to mess up a couple mortises and tenons while you figure things out that way.
Do you think I should start by just putting 2x4's and stuff together? Or do you suggest something different?

buy a book, follow a guide. Take every opportunity to learn new techniques. Just screwing together 2x4s will teach that 2x4 projects don't end up being very solid or attractive unless you're already using some more advanced joinery.

I'd say start by buying some basic woodworking HAND tools from somewhere like harbor freight where they are CHEAP. If you find yourself using them and they're breaking or not good enough, upgrade only those tools. Some things you might consider: coping saw, japanese style pull saw, miter box, speed square, chisel set, hand plane, a few clamps, wood glue, basic corded drill and wood drill bits (corded means better power/price ratio). Look up youtube videos of each tool and how it's used effectively. From there, you will start to either get ideas on projects or ideas on jigs to make.

your question is really pretty open-ended, and the answer depends a lot on what you want to make and whether you want to go down the power or hand tool (or both) path.

You don't need to buy everything to start with - pick something you want to build, and then buy the tools you need to make that. If you're buying pre-milled lumber then you can probably get away with a saw of some sort, a drill, a screw driver, a ruler a square and some glue. You can pick these all up reasonably cheaply.

A standard hobbiest shop (after a few years), would probably include most of the following: a table saw, band saw, drill press, chisels, planes, a joiner and a thicknesser and a few hand saws.

Make a book shelf. It will teach you about cutting straight and making sure corners are square. You can make it super simple with butt joints all around or try out dados and rabbits. The entire thing can be built with a circular saw(or jig saw) and a drill with a few bits and screws. Plus you built something useful.

You can build a lot with a drill, Kreg jig and a handsaw. Get some pre surfaced boards from the big box store, cut to length and put them together to make something. There's plenty of free plans out there. Check out Ana White for some beginner projects with minimal tools.

Also check out Paul Sellers' recommendations for hand tools to get started in furniture making and what joints to learn how to make. http://paulsellers.com/2014/05/questions-answered-ten-hand-tools-three-joints/
